To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extent of alteration in exercise hyperpnoea after eccentric exercise is not related to the degree of alteration of the sense of effort.
the degree of alteration of effort sense caused by neuromuscular damage induced by ECC does not significantly affect exercise hyperpnea at the beginning of exercise.
the exaggeration in exercise ventilatory response at onset of exercise after eccentric exercise (eccentric exercise-induced muscle damage) was not affected by the extent of change of effort sense.

the effect of the central command on the exercise hyperpnea after the eccentric exercise.
